text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Daewoo Heavy Industries Ltd plans to export cars made at its joint venture in Romania to East European countries.
ADEVARUL
- The leu fell by around 3.0 percent on Tuesday, a move which investors take as a sign of the reformist government's plans to bring the currency closer to real rate.
- Economic Reform Minister Ulm Spineanu said on Tuesday the government was ready to give support to the capital market.
- Romanian brewers asked the government to cut excise duties on beer by 5.0 percent to 50 percent.
TINERETUL LIBER
- Rom Telecom RA trade unions are against privatisation of the telephone company saying Romania, Rom Telecom employees and subscribers could not benefit from such a move at present.
- The number of listings on the over-the-counter (OTC) market has exceeded 1,000.
ZIUA
- The National Oil Company is expected to discuss petrol price rises on Thursday.
CRONICA ROMANA
- Tractor prices are expected to rise by 40 percent starting next year.
- Banca Agricola SA shows in an annual report that its 1995 net profit dropped to 5.0 billion lei from 26 billion the previous year.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Romcim SA, Romania's largest cement producer, entered the OTC market.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The newspaper presents the main political parties and blocs in Romania after last month's parliamentary elections.

- Romania's prosecutor general, the chairman and a judge of the constitutional court comment on parliamentary immunity and consider whether rules on conditions in which immunity can be lifted should be changed.
ADEVARUL
- The lower Chamber of Deputies on Thursday will vote on a proposal allowing the government to rule by decree during parliament's recess.
- Fifteen U.S. senators asked President Bill Clinton to include Romania into the "NATO Participation Act" to benefit of financial support to help its NATO integration in the first wave.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI

- Romania's present rulers might lose control over its government ally the Hungarian Democratic Union (UDMR) as it lacks political experience and fears to take a firm stand, says the editorial commenting on the coalition government's decision to give many public posts to UDMR representatives.

- President Emil Constantinescu will meet leaders of the Orthodox and Greek Catholic churches to mediate a conflict between the two over the restitution of Greek Catholic churches seized by the former Communists after World War Two.
- Retired parashooter Nicu Anghel was appointed the new head of the Special Protection Service (SPP) for high officials.
COTIDIANUL

- "December 1989 -- A Seven-Year-Old Puzzle" reads a front-page headline to a report on the bloody revolution which ended half a century of communist rule. ($=3,795 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
